newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kuehne & Nagel sees higher 96 profits.
newsitem.headline: Kuehne & Nagel sees higher 96 profits.

text.p: Kuehne & Nagel International AG expects to show improved profits for 1996, owner and chief executive office Klaus-Michael Kuehne said.
The international freight forwarder had a good 1996 and would exceed the planned net profit of 63 million Swiss francs, he said in an interview with the German financial newspaper Handelsblatt.
Kuehne & Nagel made net profits of 59.2 million francs in 1995 on a turnover of five billion francs.
In Europe, business in Scandinavia and southern Europe was unsatisfactory and medium-term priority would be given to expansion in EU countries, Kuehne said.
The company invested 44.4 million francs in the first half of 1996, including in a Rotterdam container terminal and logistics centres in Belgium, Britain and Luxembourg.
Kuehne said the forwarder's global presence with 470 offices in 82 countries gave it a competitive advantage over airlines and shipping companies by being able to offer complete logistics services.
Airlines and integrators alone could only offer global door-to-door services in part, he said.
Kuehne & Nagel had sufficient purchasing power to buy up air and sea cargo capacity months in advance on the basis of client contracts, he noted.
In addition, international air cargo shippers could save money by outsourcing responsibility for supply chain management to forwarders with global networks, Kuehne added.
